[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Parameters in Stored Procedures"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Stored procedures are precompiled SQL code blocks that can be executed by name. They are beneficial for code reusability, improved performance, and enhanced security. Parameters allow you to pass values into stored procedures, making them more flexible and dynamic. This tutorial will cover the different types of parameters, how to define them, and how to use them effectively."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Types of Parameters"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"SQL Server supports three types of parameters in stored procedures:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Input Parameters: Used to pass values into the stored procedure. These are the most common type of parameter."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Output Parameters: Used to return values from the stored procedure. The stored procedure modifies the value of the parameter, and the calling program can access the updated value."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Input/Output Parameters: A combination of input and output parameters. A value is passed into the stored procedure, and the stored procedure can modify and return the value."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Defining Input Parameters"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Input parameters are defined within the `CREATE PROCEDURE` statement. Each parameter requires a name, data type, and optionally, a default value. The `@` symbol prefixes the parameter name."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"CREATE PROCEDURE GetProductByName
    @ProductName VARCHAR(50)
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT * FROM Products WHERE ProductName LIKE '%' + @ProductName + '%'
END"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the above example, `@ProductName` is an input parameter of type `VARCHAR(50)`. The stored procedure `GetProductByName` retrieves products whose name contains the value passed in the `@ProductName` parameter."},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"To execute the stored procedure, use the `EXEC` or `EXECUTE` statement:"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"EXEC GetProductByName 'Keyboard'"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Defining Output Parameters"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Output parameters are defined using the `OUTPUT` keyword in the `CREATE PROCEDURE` statement. They must also be declared in the calling program to receive the returned value."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"CREATE PROCEDURE GetProductCount
    @CategoryName VARCHAR(50),
    @ProductCount INT OUTPUT
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT @ProductCount = COUNT(*) FROM Products WHERE Category = @CategoryName
END"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, `@ProductCount` is an output parameter of type `INT`. The stored procedure `GetProductCount` counts the number of products in a given category and returns the count through the `@ProductCount` parameter."},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"To execute this stored procedure and retrieve the output value:"},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"DECLARE @Count INT
EXEC GetProductCount 'Electronics', @Count OUTPUT
SELECT @Count AS ProductCount"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here, a variable `@Count` is declared to store the output value. The `OUTPUT` keyword is used when executing the stored procedure to indicate that `@Count` will receive the value from the `@ProductCount` parameter. Finally, the value of `@Count` is displayed."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Defining Input/Output Parameters"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Input/Output parameters combine the functionality of both input and output parameters. They are defined using the `OUTPUT` keyword, and a value can be passed in, modified within the stored procedure, and then returned."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"CREATE PROCEDURE FormatPhoneNumber
    @PhoneNumber VARCHAR(20) OUTPUT
AS
BEGIN
    SET @PhoneNumber = '(' + SUBSTRING(@PhoneNumber, 1, 3) + ') ' + SUBSTRING(@PhoneNumber, 4, 3) + '-' + SUBSTRING(@PhoneNumber, 7, 4)
END"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, `@PhoneNumber` is an input/output parameter. The stored procedure `FormatPhoneNumber` takes a phone number as input, formats it, and returns the formatted phone number through the same parameter."},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"To execute this stored procedure:"},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"DECLARE @Phone VARCHAR(20) = '1234567890'
EXEC FormatPhoneNumber @Phone OUTPUT
SELECT @Phone AS FormattedPhoneNumber"},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"The variable `@Phone` is initialized with the unformatted phone number. After executing the stored procedure, `@Phone` will contain the formatted phone number."},{"order":28,"type":"subheading","text":"Default Parameter Values"},{"order":29,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can assign default values to input parameters. If a value is not provided when executing the stored procedure, the default value will be used."},{"order":30,"type":"code","text":"CREATE PROCEDURE GetProductsByPriceRange
    @MinPrice DECIMAL(10, 2) = 0,
    @MaxPrice DECIMAL(10, 2) = 100
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT * FROM Products WHERE Price BETWEEN @MinPrice AND @MaxPrice
END"},{"order":31,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, `@MinPrice` defaults to 0 and `@MaxPrice` defaults to 100. If you execute `EXEC GetProductsByPriceRange`, it will retrieve products with prices between 0 and 100. You can override these defaults by providing values, e.g., `EXEC GetProductsByPriceRange 50, 200`."},{"order":32,"type":"subheading","text":"Benefits of Using Parameters"},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Code Reusability: Stored procedures with parameters can be used with different input values, reducing code duplication."},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Improved Performance: Stored procedures are precompiled, and using parameters allows the database engine to reuse execution plans, improving performance."},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enhanced Security: Parameters help prevent SQL injection attacks by treating input values as data rather than executable code."},{"order":36,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":37,"type":"paragraph","text":"Parameters are a crucial aspect of stored procedures, allowing for dynamic and reusable SQL code. Understanding the different types of parameters and how to use them effectively is essential for developing robust and efficient database applications."}]
